# Code tools

Native code: ahead-of-time compiled behaviors and C++ modules (trusted local code; clients ask first).

4 tools in the `code` category. Badges: **read-only** tools never change the project; **mutating** tools are undoable and attributed; **open-world** tools reach outside the engine and MCP clients ask before running them.

| Tool | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`wander_compile_native`](#wander_compile_native) | AOT-compile Wander behaviors to C++ and load them as native code (system clang++, cached by program hash, so unchanged behaviors load instantly). |
| [`native_build`](#native_build) | Compile the project's native C++ module (native/*.cpp against skywalker/native/sdk.h, plus flags, include dirs, libraries, frameworks and pkg-config packages from native/module.json) into a library with the system clang++, then load it: its builtins become callable from every behavior (they appear in wander_reference) and its systems run every tick while playing. |
| [`native_list`](#native_list) | Status of the project's native code: whether native sources exist, the C++ compiler, the last build and its diagnostics, the loaded module with its builtins (signatures) and systems, and behaviors running as AOT-compiled native code. |
| [`native_template`](#native_template) | Write a starter native module: native/&lt;name&gt;.cpp (a builtin `wave(t, freq)` and a per-tick system that spins entities tagged "spinner") and native/module.json (flags, include_dirs, lib_dirs, libs, frameworks, pkg_config). |

### `wander_compile_native` { #wander_compile_native }

**Compile behaviors to native code** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

AOT-compile Wander behaviors to C++ and load them as native code (system clang++, cached by program hash, so unchanged behaviors load instantly). Native code has identical semantics (same results, errors and step budget) and runs hot loops several times faster; anything that fails to build keeps running in the VM. Pass entity to compile its behaviors, or nothing for every behavior in the scene. auto=true compiles every behavior automatically whenever play starts. Edited behaviors fall back to the VM until compiled again.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Only this entity's behaviors |  |
| `force` | boolean |  | Rebuild even if a cached library exists |  |
| `auto` | boolean |  | Compile all behaviors natively at every play start |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    wander_compile_native {"entity": "Swarm", "force": false}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call wander_compile_native '{"entity": "Swarm", "force": false}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "wander_compile_native",
        "arguments": {
          "entity": "Swarm",
          "force": false
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `native_build` { #native_build }

**Build native module** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Compile the project's native C++ module (native/*.cpp against skywalker/native/sdk.h, plus flags, include dirs, libraries, frameworks and pkg-config packages from native/module.json) into a library with the system clang++, then load it: its builtins become callable from every behavior (they appear in wander_reference) and its systems run every tick while playing. Compiler errors come back as structured diagnostics {file, line, column, message} relative to the project. Unchanged sources load the cached build instantly. Security: this runs native code you or an agent wrote inside the engine; review it first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `force` | boolean |  | Rebuild even if nothing changed |  |
| `load` | boolean |  | Load the module after a successful build (default true) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    native_build {"force": true}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call native_build '{"force": true}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "native_build",
        "arguments": {
          "force": true
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `native_list` { #native_list }

**Native module status** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Status of the project's native code: whether native sources exist, the C++ compiler, the last build and its diagnostics, the loaded module with its builtins (signatures) and systems, and behaviors running as AOT-compiled native code.

Takes no arguments.

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    native_list {}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call native_list '{}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "native_list",
        "arguments": {}
      }
    }
    ```

### `native_template` { #native_template }

**Create native module** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Write a starter native module: native/<name>.cpp (a builtin `wave(t, freq)` and a per-tick system that spins entities tagged "spinner") and native/module.json (flags, include_dirs, lib_dirs, libs, frameworks, pkg_config). Edit it, then native_build. Use it for hot inner loops (flocking, procedural generation, custom physics) or to bring in any C++ library (e.g. Homebrew packages via pkg_config).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | File name without extension (default "gameplay") |  |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | Replace an existing file |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    native_template {"name": "gameplay", "overwrite": false}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call native_template '{"name": "gameplay", "overwrite": false}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "native_template",
        "arguments": {
          "name": "gameplay",
          "overwrite": false
        }
      }
    }
    ```
